My mission is to make building and sharing technology easy, accessible, and sustainable.

I strongly advocate for the principles of open-source, the maker movement, and the right-to-repair, all of which center around empowering users to have control over and a deep understanding of the technology they rely on.

From research group to runtime

Most of my work follows one line, from university research to an open hardware standard, the software that drives it, and a company.

FAST Research Group

Free Appropriate Sustainable Technology, Western University. Open-source scientific equipment and lab hardware; I maintain most of the group's public repositories.

FEAST

An open ecosystem for building modular automation devices, continuing the BREAD hardware standard. I lead its engineering: the standard, its CI, and the CRUMBS messaging protocol.

Anolis

A capability-oriented machine control runtime, developed and validated against FEAST hardware. In active development.

Integrum Systems Inc.

The systems-integration company I founded in 2026.

Other organizations

heibench

Hardware Engineering Integration bench: drive existing engineering engines programmatically and check output against declared intent.

FiberPath

Planning, simulating, and executing filament-winding jobs for precise, repeatable composite parts.

baseliner

Portable assessment-as-code for repository fleets: one binary, no server, no app.

Konnexio Inc.

Custom machine builder in London, Ontario, specializing in adapto™ modular assembly line construction.

Principles

Accessibility & Collaboration

Lowering the barriers to building, sharing, and maintaining technology: open tools and documentation that others can pick up, use, and extend.

Composability and Modularity

Designing hardware and software as modular, recombinable parts with clear interfaces, so systems can be assembled and adapted across domains.
